executive_summary: A bypassed EXEC-TO-PLAN handoff (handoff.js execute EXEC-TO-PLAN --bypass-validation) is currently byte-identical, on every row downstream gates and roles read, to a genuinely validated one -- because the one real choke point (BaseExecutor.js's bypass fall-through, at two sites) logs a warning and falls straight into the success return without mutating the result object, so gateResults.passed=false never survives into HandoffRecorder.js. Two SDs (SD-LEO-FIX-HUMAN-ACTION-FENCES-001 and others) reached status=completed on a BLOCKED required TESTING verdict this way. This SD stamps the bypass at its origin, persists that stamp faithfully through the recorder into both leo_handoff_executions and sd_phase_handoffs, adds a per-SD LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL refusal when any phase in the chain carries an unresolved bypass, fixes the SD-linkage gap on the audit-log side of a key-invoked bypass, narrowly corrects advisory-mode sub-agent evidence handling so a BLOCKED required verdict can never read as a pass, and builds the guarded, audited path to uncomplete the false completions already on record.

functional_requirements.title: Stamp bypassed:true on the result at the real choke point
functional_requirements.description: scripts/modules/handoff/executors/BaseExecutor.js has two sites (~line 348, the coordinator-authority fence bypass; and ~lines 641-649/820-830, the general gate-failure bypass under options.bypassValidation) where a required-gate failure is logged to stdout and execution falls through into the success return WITHOUT the returned result object recording that a bypass occurred. Add result.bypassed = true (plus result.bypassReason and result.bypassedGates, the list of gate names that were failing when the bypass fired) at both sites. This does NOT change control flow -- execution still proceeds under bypass exactly as today; only the result's truthfulness changes.
acceptance_criteria: A handoff run with --bypass-validation over a gate_results set containing a required:true failure returns/persists a result with bypassed===true
A handoff run with NO bypass flag and all required gates passing is unaffected: bypassed is absent/false, existing behavior unchanged

functional_requirements.title: Persist the bypass stamp faithfully in HandoffRecorder (both persisted rows)
functional_requirements.description: lib/handoff/HandoffRecorder.js's recordSuccess() (writing leo_handoff_executions) hardcodes validation_passed: true regardless of result.bypassed, and never records a bypassed field. The separate sd_phase_handoffs insert (same file) computes validation_passed: result.success !== false, also ignoring result.bypassed. Fix BOTH: when result.bypassed===true, leo_handoff_executions.validation_passed must be false (or a distinct value never read as 'passed' by any downstream consumer) and the row must carry the bypass stamp (bypassReason, bypassedGates) in its own metadata/validation_details field; the HandoffRecorder scoreSource computation (currently only 'measured'/'not_measured') gains a third value 'bypassed', used whenever result.bypassed===true regardless of the numeric score. Apply the identical correction to the sd_phase_handoffs insert's validation_passed derivation and stamp metadata.bypass = { reason, actor, gates, bypassed_at } on that row (this is the field FR-4's LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL check reads). Executors that already correctly self-stamp bypassed:true on their own result (plan-to-exec/index.js, grill-convergence.js, activation-invariant-gate.js, integration-contract-gate.js) must now have that stamp actually survive into both rows, since today the recorder drops it regardless of source.
acceptance_criteria: leo_handoff_executions.validation_passed is never true for a row where the executor result carried bypassed===true
sd_phase_handoffs.metadata.bypass is populated (reason, actor, gates, bypassed_at) whenever the corresponding handoff was bypassed
A genuinely passing (non-bypassed) handoff's leo_handoff_executions.validation_passed and sd_phase_handoffs.validation_passed are unchanged from current behavior

functional_requirements.title: Fix SD linkage on the validation_audit_log emission for a key-invoked bypass
functional_requirements.description: scripts/modules/handoff/cli/cli-main.js already resolves an SD key to its UUID correctly before the bypass_ledger insert, but the paired emitValidationAuditLog(...) call (~line 785) is not given that resolved UUID when the CLI was invoked with an SD KEY rather than a UUID -- and validation_audit_log has no sd_key column at all, so the audit row lands with sd_id=NULL and zero SD linkage. Resolve the SD identifier to its UUID once, before EITHER write, and pass the resolved UUID to both the bypass_ledger insert and the emitValidationAuditLog call.
acceptance_criteria: Invoking handoff.js execute <PHASE> <SD-KEY> --bypass-validation (SD KEY form, not UUID) produces a validation_audit_log row with a non-null sd_id matching the SD
The existing UUID-invocation form continues to produce a correctly-linked row (no regression)

functional_requirements.title: LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL refuses completion while any phase in the SD's chain was bypassed without a linked follow-up
functional_requirements.description: scripts/modules/handoff/executors/lead-final-approval/gates/learning-or-bypass-resolved-gate.js is the only existing per-SD-scoped bypass-aware LEAD-FINAL gate, but it reads validation_audit_log filtered on validator_name IN ('bypass_rubric','bypass_shape') and is warn-only by default (ENFORCE_LEARNING_GATE=false) -- a different signal than the sd_phase_handoffs.metadata.bypass stamp FR-2 introduces. Add a NEW, clearly-separated check inside this gate (or a sibling gate function, kept in the same file to avoid a second registration): read every sd_phase_handoffs row for this SD where metadata.bypass is present, and REFUSE completion (real failure, not warn-only) unless every such bypass carries a linked follow-up per the existing --pattern-id/--followup-sd-key shape already enforced at bypass time by bypass-rubric.js (ENFORCE_BYPASS_SHAPE, already flipped true). Keep this as an independent code path from the existing validator_name-based check so the two signals are never conflated.
acceptance_criteria: LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL fails (not warns) for an SD carrying an unresolved bypass (no linked --pattern-id/--followup-sd-key) anywhere in its phase chain
LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL passes normally for an SD whose bypasses (if any) all carry a linked follow-up, and for an SD with no bypasses at all
The existing validator_name-based (bypass_rubric/bypass_shape) check in the same gate file is unmodified and continues to run

functional_requirements.title: Guarded, audited path to uncomplete a false completion
functional_requirements.description: scripts/reactivate-sd.js today only reopens an SD from status='deferred' (VALID_REACTIVATION_TARGETS already includes 'active'; TERMINAL_STATUSES only decorates the refusal message, it does not independently gate). Add a second, narrowly-guarded branch: allow status='completed' -> 'active' at current_phase='LEAD_FINAL', ONLY when the SD's metadata.completion_evidence_invalid === true. On success: clear completion_date, write an sd_transition_audit row (transition_type='UNCOMPLETE_FALSE_PASS', pre_state/post_state as the existing buildReactivationAudit shape already does) capturing who/why/the offending handoff id, and leave metadata.completion_evidence_invalid in place (not cleared) as a durable marker that this SD was once falsely completed. Refuse (with a clear reason) when status='completed' and the flag is absent/false -- do not silently no-op. Because metadata.completion_evidence_invalid has no existing writer anywhere in the codebase, this SD must ALSO add a minimal, audited setter (a new small script, e.g. scripts/mark-completion-evidence-invalid.js) that a coordinator/operator runs with --sd-id and --reason to set the flag (and itself writes an audit trail entry), so the reopen path in reactivate-sd.js is reachable rather than dead by construction.
acceptance_criteria: reactivate-sd.js --to active on a status='completed' SD with metadata.completion_evidence_invalid=true succeeds: status becomes 'active', current_phase becomes 'LEAD_FINAL', completion_date is cleared, and an sd_transition_audit row is written
reactivate-sd.js --to active on a status='completed' SD WITHOUT that flag is refused exactly as today (no new silent success path)
scripts/mark-completion-evidence-invalid.js sets the flag on a given SD with an auditable reason, and refuses without a --reason

functional_requirements.title: Advisory verdict_mode never converts a BLOCKED/rejecting required sub-agent verdict into a pass
functional_requirements.description: scripts/modules/handoff/gates/subagent-evidence-gate.js resolveSubagentVerdictMode() defaults to 'advisory' for every SD (not bugfix-scoped as the originating report assumed). In advisory mode, a BLOCKED verdict on a required sub-agent currently returns passed:true, score:100 (~lines 621-630) -- an in-code comment measures this affects 32/313 SDs. Narrowly correct this: advisory mode may continue to soften MISSING evidence (no verdict recorded at all) to a pass, but a REJECTING verdict (BLOCKED, FAIL, or any non-passing recorded verdict) on a required sub-agent must never be converted to passed:true under advisory mode -- it fails the gate exactly as block mode would. This is a correctness fix to the advisory softening, not a change to the advisory/block default itself, and its blast radius must be independently assessed by the SECURITY sub-agent at EXEC-TO-PLAN (this SD's fresh_security_evidence_required flag) given the 32-SD figure.
acceptance_criteria: Advisory mode + a required sub-agent recorded with a BLOCKED verdict => gate fails (passed:false), not passed:true/score:100
Advisory mode + a required sub-agent with NO recorded verdict at all (missing evidence) => existing softened-pass behavior is unchanged
Block mode (SUBAGENT_VERDICT_MODE=block) behavior is completely unchanged by this fix

functional_requirements.title: Regression tests proving the false-completion class is closed
functional_requirements.description: Build/reconstruct a gate_results fixture equivalent to the SD-LEO-FIX-HUMAN-ACTION-FENCES-001 handoff row 1a1b3087 (45 gates, MANDATORY_TESTING_VALIDATION and 2D:testingSubAgentVerified both failing, required:true) and prove it is rejected end-to-end through the real accept path (bypassed and stamped as such, never persisted as validation_passed=true) whether reached via a plain failing run, the preflight-remediation retry route, or an explicit --bypass-validation invocation. Also prove a genuinely passing fixture still accepts normally (no regression), and that a bugfix SD carrying a BLOCKED TESTING verdict anywhere in its chain cannot reach status='completed' end-to-end (LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL refuses per FR-4).
acceptance_criteria: The 1a1b3087-equivalent fixture is rejected/stamped-bypassed on every route exercised by the test suite
A genuinely passing 45-gate fixture still results in an accepted, non-bypassed handoff
An end-to-end test drives a bugfix SD with a BLOCKED required TESTING verdict through to LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL and asserts refusal

technical_requirements.title: No schema migration required
technical_requirements.description: sd_phase_handoffs.metadata and strategic_directives_v2.metadata are both existing JSONB columns; the new bypass and completion_evidence_invalid keys are additive JSONB fields, not new columns. leo_handoff_executions gains no new column either -- the bypass stamp reuses its existing validation_details/metadata JSONB field.

technical_requirements.title: Reuse existing bypass infrastructure, no new tables or flags
technical_requirements.description: Reuse bypass_ledger, ENFORCE_BYPASS_SHAPE (already true in the root .env per Adam's fleet rule), and the existing --pattern-id/--followup-sd-key shape enforcement. No new environment flag is introduced by FR-1 through FR-5; FR-6 is a logic correction inside the existing advisory branch, not a new flag.

technical_requirements.title: Forward-looking only, no retroactive backfill in this SD's scope
technical_requirements.description: This SD fixes the mechanism going forward. It does not retroactively re-stamp or re-score the ~43/439 already-completed SDs that carry a bypass mark, or the specific false-completion specimens (SD-LEO-FIX-HUMAN-ACTION-FENCES-001 etc.) -- those are uncompleted via FR-5's guarded path as a separate, explicit operator action per specimen, tracked outside this SD.

risks.risk: HandoffRecorder.js's validation_passed derivation is read by many existing consumers; a change scoped too broadly could regress passing handoffs
risks.mitigation: The change is strictly additive/conditional: validation_passed only differs from today's value when result.bypassed===true. A non-bypassed successful run's derivation and output are byte-identical to current behavior, covered by TS-4/TS-12.

risks.risk: Extending gates/learning-or-bypass-resolved-gate.js risks conflating the new sd_phase_handoffs.metadata.bypass check with the existing validation_audit_log-based check
risks.mitigation: Implement the new check as an independently-testable code path within the same file (kept as one gate registration), never merging the two signals into a single conditional.

risks.risk: FR-6's advisory-mode correctness fix touches a path affecting an estimated 32/313 SDs; narrowing it incorrectly could newly fail SDs that were passing on a softened BLOCKED verdict
risks.mitigation: Scope strictly to REJECTING verdicts (BLOCKED/FAIL); the MISSING-evidence softening path is explicitly left untouched. Fresh SECURITY sub-agent evidence is required at EXEC-TO-PLAN specifically to independently assess this blast radius before merge.

risks.risk: metadata.completion_evidence_invalid has no existing writer; FR-5's reopen path is unreachable unless the setter script is also built in this SD
risks.mitigation: FR-5 explicitly includes scripts/mark-completion-evidence-invalid.js as in-scope deliverable, not a follow-up, closing the dead-by-construction gap identified during LEAD validation.

consumers: The LEO Protocol handoff pipeline for every future SD/QF phase transition (EXEC-TO-PLAN, PLAN-TO-LEAD, LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL and any other bypass-eligible handoff)
Coordinator/chairman tooling and dashboards that read sd_phase_handoffs/leo_handoff_executions to assess completion integrity
Any future gate or report that wants a trustworthy per-SD bypass signal (now sourced from sd_phase_handoffs.metadata.bypass rather than reconstructed ad hoc)
dependencies: bypass_ledger table and its existing insert path in cli-main.js (unchanged shape, only the SD-linkage fix in FR-3)
ENFORCE_BYPASS_SHAPE flag (already flipped true in the root .env by Adam per the chairman root-cause directive)
SUBAGENT_VERDICT_MODE / subagent-evidence-gate.js advisory/block infrastructure (unchanged default, FR-6 is a logic correction inside the existing advisory branch)
data_contracts: sd_phase_handoffs.metadata gains an additive JSONB key 'bypass' ({reason, actor, gates, bypassed_at}) -- no column/migration change
strategic_directives_v2.metadata gains an additive JSONB key 'completion_evidence_invalid' (boolean) -- no column/migration change
leo_handoff_executions gains no new column; the bypass stamp is carried in its existing validation_details/metadata JSONB field with a new scoreSource value 'bypassed'
runtime_config: No new environment flags introduced. Reuses ENFORCE_BYPASS_SHAPE (already true) and the existing SUBAGENT_VERDICT_MODE default (unchanged).
observability_rollout: New fields are visible immediately on the next handoff run after merge -- verified by the unit/integration tests in FR-7/TS-1..TS-12

Live verification against the real false-completion specimens (e.g. SD-LEO-FIX-HUMAN-ACTION-FENCES-001) happens via FR-5's guarded uncomplete path as a separate, explicit operator action once this SD ships -- not a blocking step of this SD's own EXEC/PLAN-TO-LEAD/LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL cycle

system_architecture.summary: One choke-point fix (BaseExecutor.js) whose stamp is threaded through the existing recorder (HandoffRecorder.js) into both persisted rows, read back by a new per-SD check in an existing LEAD-FINAL gate, paired with a small SD-linkage fix in the CLI's audit emission, a narrow advisory-mode correctness fix, and a new guarded/audited reopen path plus its setter script.

implementation_approach.summary: Fix the truth at its source (BaseExecutor), make the recorder honest about it (HandoffRecorder, both persisted rows), close the one linkage gap in the CLI's audit emission, teach the one existing per-SD LEAD-FINAL gate to refuse on an unresolved bypass, narrowly correct the advisory-mode softening bug, and build the audited path to undo a false completion plus the setter that makes it reachable -- in that dependency order so each step is testable against the previous one's real output.
steps: FR-1: BaseExecutor.js stamps bypassed on the result (both sites) -- unit-tested in isolation first, since every later step depends on this signal existing
FR-2: HandoffRecorder.js reads and persists the stamp on both leo_handoff_executions and sd_phase_handoffs -- unit-tested against FR-1's real stamped result shape
FR-3: cli-main.js SD-linkage fix for the audit-log emission -- independent, can land in parallel with FR-2
FR-4: extend gates/learning-or-bypass-resolved-gate.js to read FR-2's sd_phase_handoffs.metadata.bypass and refuse completion -- depends on FR-2 being in place
FR-6: narrow advisory-mode correctness fix in subagent-evidence-gate.js -- independent of FR-1/2/3/4, can land in parallel; SECURITY sub-agent evidence gathered for this step specifically

FR-5: reactivate-sd.js guarded reopen branch plus scripts/mark-completion-evidence-invalid.js -- independent, but logically closes the loop opened by FR-4 (an SD that FR-4 would now correctly refuse to complete, or was falsely completed before this SD shipped, needs an undo path)
FR-7: regression tests proving the 1a1b3087-equivalent fixture is rejected on every route and a genuinely passing fixture is unaffected, plus the end-to-end LEAD-FINAL-APPROVAL refusal test
